subject: Observability export: on-prem routing, sampling, and Splunk HEC fingerprinting
messages:
From: Aaron Patel <aaron@acmehealth.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Observability handoff: Splunk onramp & retention constraints

Hi Hannah / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached are our Splunk requirements and a simple network diagram. Our security team needs a short design describing how Redwood will: 
- deliver logs and metrics from the private deployment to our Splunk HEC endpoints,
- guarantee zero plaintext egress (allowlist-only TLS),
- preserve tracing context for distributed traces (we use W3C), and
- provide evidence of retention and deletion for audits.

Constraints:
- No outbound internet except to pre-approved IPs; egress is via a firewall that only allows TCP 8088/443 with mutual TLS.
- We require token rotation and KMS-based wrapping for HEC tokens.
- Sampling should be configurable by route/model so we don't overwhelm our SIEM during bursts.

Can you send a proposed wiring and a short set of hard requirements we can hand to our infra team? We want to schedule a 1-hour test window next week to prove end-to-end forwarding.

Thanks,
Aaron
Aaron Patel
SRE Lead, Observability
AcmeHealth

Attachments: acme_splunk_requirements.pdf, acme-network-diagram.png

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Aaron Patel <aaron@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability handoff: Splunk onramp & retention constraints

Aaron — thanks for the clarity and the attachments. Below is a concise proposal we can hand to your infra/security team, plus a couple of open decisions we need your sign-off on. If this looks good I’ll turn it into a one-page checklist and a follow-up runbook for the test window.

Proposed wiring (high level):
- Collector topology: deploy a local agent (Fluentd/Vector) in the VPC on each inference node set + a centralized forwarder in the customer data subnet. Agents write to local disk, forward to the centralized forwarder over mTLS.
- Forwarding: centralized forwarder → Splunk HEC (TLS) using mutual TLS + client cert pinning. HEC endpoint must be reachable on the firewall allowlist. If HEC is unreachable, forwarder will buffer to encrypted object store (S3-compatible) inside the VPC; retention there is controlled by your lifecycle policy.
- Authentication: HEC tokens wrapped by customer KMS (we will not store plaintext tokens). Tokens are presented by the forwarder and rotated on a schedule you control (we support rotation hooks).
- Index/tenant isolation: use per-tenant HEC inputs + index routing at the forwarder. Use Splunk metadata fields for model, route, and environment to support retention and search scoping.
- Sampling & throttling: sampling rules are policy-configurable by inference route and by token bucket (burst + sustained rate). We will sample traces (W3C) at the SDK level and provide a configurable tail-sampling option at the forwarder so you can keep representative traces for quality while reducing SIEM load.
- Tracing hooks: we preserve W3C traceparent/tracestate; Redwood’s tracehook will annotate spans with model_id, session_id, and inference_latency_ms. Span export uses OTLP over gRPC to a collector that then converts to Splunk APM format (if you prefer Splunk traces) or keeps OTLP for your tracing backend.
- Evidence & audit: every forwarder exposes an audit log (hash-chained) for export; retention/deletion requests can be served via the evidence API and we will provide a signed manifest describing exported files and deletion timestamps.

Open decisions / asks for Acme infra:
1) Confirm allowed egress IPs for HEC and whether DNS-based hostnames are permitted (we prefer DNS with cert validation; allowlist IPs are required if your firewall does L7 block).
2) Confirm the KMS method (customer-managed AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault, or HSM) for wrapping HEC tokens.
3) Retention SLA target for raw logs in Splunk and in the fallback object store (e.g., 90 days hot, 365 days cold?).

Test plan (can be run in a 60-minute window):
- 10m: handshake and validate client certs + firewall connectivity.
- 20m: push synthetic logs + traces at burst rate; validate HEC ingestion and indexing.
- 20m: simulate HEC outage and validate fallback buffering to encrypted object store, then re-ingest.
- 10m: confirm rotation flow for HEC tokens and generate audit manifest.

Attachments we will provide for the runbook: example client cert chain, forwarder config snippet (Fluentd/Vector), sample OTLP tracehook config.

I’ll need answers to the three open decisions above before we finalize the runbook. Happy to hop on a call with your infra team — suggest Wed 26 May 09:00-10:00 PT.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Principal Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

Adding a few technical clarifications and constraints we need to lock down before the test: 

- Egress/protocol specifics: Splunk HEC accepts TLS on 8088 or 443. We support both but your firewall must permit the chosen port and allow mTLS client cert verification. If your firewall only allows 443 with SNI checking we need to ensure SNI matches the HEC hostname.
- Fingerprinting concern: to satisfy security, we'll implement a HEC fingerprint check on the forwarder side (compare server cert fingerprint to the expected value) — this avoids DNS poisoning risks if your network team prefers IP pinning + cert fingerprint as a double-check.
- Buffering & storage: the forwarder writes to encrypted local tiers first (fast write), then to the VPC object store for safekeeping. The object store must support lifecycle policies we can reference in audit logs.
- Fallback ingestion: if HEC <-> forwarder fails, we will keep encrypted bundles and expose a signed manifest URL for retrieval. Optionally Redwood can re-ingest into Splunk via a temporary per-test credential during the remediation window.
- Metrics shipping: metrics are sent via OTLP metric export in batches; recommended max batch size during bursts: 1000 pts / 60s per forwarder (configurable).

Security ask: we will need a short service-account cert CN naming convention and a list of acceptable CAs (or your root cert) to embed in the forwarder image before the test.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Infrastructure & Security PM
Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah & Kimberly — this looks promising and addresses most of our asks. A couple quick replies and next steps: 

- Egress: we will permit DNS to the HEC hostname (preferred), but we will provide IPs for firewall rules as a fallback. We'll also provide the server cert fingerprint after we test with our network team.
- KMS: we use AWS KMS in our VPC; we will produce a key policy that allows the forwarder role to unwrap tokens.
- Retention: target is 90 days searchable in Splunk with a 7-year cold archive in GUIDed object storage. Please include retention markers in the audit manifest.
- Test window: Wed 26 May 09:00-10:00 PT works for us. Please send calendar invite and the runbook.

Attached is a sample HEC token file (redacted) for the test and a pointer to our Splunk HEC docs. We will create a temporary test input and rotate it after the test.

Appreciate the clear plan — looking forward to the runbook.

Best,
Aaron
